title: Typed payload contracts and robust chunk-reassembly helpers for Python SDK streaming responses
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Developers need easy, reliable patterns to consume partially emitted LLM outputs where structured objects (e.g., JSON payloads, proto-like records) can be split across chunk boundaries. Current examples either reassemble raw bytes manually or eagerly validate every partial fragment, which is error-prone and slow.

Goal: Ship a small, well-documented set of typed payload contracts plus ergonomic iterator helpers that: (1) allow dataclass-first models with optional Pydantic adapters, (2) incrementally reassemble chunked payloads into strongly-typed objects, (3) provide safe retry hooks when a chunk stream is interrupted mid-object, and (4) remain performant for high-throughput production workloads.

Scope: Python SDK only (this ticket focuses on API surface + core implementation + examples). Follow-up tickets will adapt the same patterns to TypeScript and Go.

Deliverables: library code exposing a CompactEnvelope contract, IncrementalDeserializer/AsyncChunkAssembler helpers, an adapter layer for Pydantic and dataclasses, a retryable-consume wrapper that exposes idempotent resume tokens, unit + integration tests, and two example cookbooks (simple chat streaming + structured record ingestion).
acceptance_criteria: Public API: CompactEnvelope (string: envelope_type, str: partial, optional: boundary_marker) documented
Public API: AsyncChunkAssembler that yields fully-formed typed objects (dataclass instances) from async iterators of raw stream chunks
Adapter: simple function to convert dataclass definitions to optional Pydantic model for validation without forcing Pydantic at callsites
Retry semantics: resume token surface that callers can persist and pass to retryable_consume() to continue from the last confirmed object without duplicating emitted objects
Performance: reassembly + minimal validation path adds <8% latency vs raw reassembly in our microbenchmark at 1k/s streams
Examples: two worked examples merged into /examples/streaming/structured_ingest.py and /examples/streaming/chat_structured_output.py
Tests: 100% coverage for boundary reconciliation logic and deterministic behavior for truncated-chunk scenarios
Docs: short migration notes for teams using previous ad-hoc reassembly code and a recommended pattern section in SDK cookbook
updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created after discussion in SDK weekly (design doc linked). Decided to pursue dataclass-first ergonomics with optional Pydantic adapters to minimize runtime dependency weight for light users.

2026-03-11: Spike implemented proving async iterator parquet-like reassembly; found two failure modes: (1) boundary marker collisions when payload contains marker bytes, (2) partial JSON objects across chunk boundaries leading to invalid incremental parsing. Proposal: use CompactEnvelope with explicit length prefixes for production streams and fall back to marker-aware reassembly for best-effort compatibility.

2026-03-11: Design decision: validation will be lazy by default (validate complete objects only) with opt-in strict mode that validates incremental fragments for users that need stronger safety guarantees.

2026-03-12: PR draft opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-py/pull/2377 implementing AsyncChunkAssembler + dataclass->pydantic adapter. Requesting initial review from @maria-ops and @cheng-li. Benchmarks attached.

2026-03-12: Engineering review feedback: prefer simple tuple resume token (stream_id, last_seq_n) rather than embedding offsets; simplifies cross-language resume semantics. Updated acceptance criteria accordingly.
